title: Garden of Focus — two-week momentum log
content:
Purpose:
This is a lightweight two-week personal momentum log — a scratchpad for tracking micro-KPIs, daily focus slots, and quick retros after sprints. Not a formal plan; the goal is to capture what actually gets done, why, and one small experiment each cycle.

How I use this:
- Quick morning check (3 minutes): scan scorecard, pick the single priority for the day.
- Evening micro-retro (5 minutes): note what helped, what blocked, one adjustment.
- Weekly review (20–30 minutes): synthesize and update next two-week priorities.

QUICK SCORECARD (current two-week window):
- Primary metric (engineering impact): reduce 95th-percentile model-response latency on hosted-prod by 12% (baseline: 420ms) -> target: 370ms.
- Secondary metric (productivity): 3 merged PRs touching routing/cache code; unblock 1 high-priority customer ticket.
- Personal health: keep 4 focus-slots of 60–90 mins each week (Pomodoro-ish).

Concrete experiments to run this window:
1) Prefix caching audit: add logging around KV-hit-rate for route X (JIRA-ENG-2345).
   - Hypothesis: adding a small TTL bump (2->4 min) will increase hit-rate and reduce tail latency.
   - Acceptance: measurable +5% KV hit-rate and ~5–10% tail latency improvement in staging.
2) Latency budget guard: add a tiny adaptive-batching gate that favors low-latency tails during peak times.
   - Track via temporary dashboard (see linked Confluence playbook).
3) PR blitz: chunk a larger refactor into 3 small PRs; aim to merge 2 by week end to reduce review fatigue.

DAILY/SESSION NOTES (scratchy, unordered)
- 2025-01-07 morning: picked priority = prefix cache logging. Spent 45 mins instrumenting. Found old debug flag set; weird.
- 2025-01-08: small spike in staging (time-series shows higher variance after longer sequences). Flagging to SRE.
- 2025-01-09 afternoon: pair with Riley for 30m on batching heuristics. Idea: bias sampler away from long-history sequences during high QPS.

PRIORITY TODO (short list)
- [ ] Finish cache instrumentation and push to canary. (ptr: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/812)
- [ ] Create staging comparison dashboard: 95th/99th latency, KV hit-rate, request-size histogram.
- [ ] Break refactor into PR A/B/C; open PR A.
- [ ] Draft short note to Customer Success about potential customer impact (CS-ops).

RETRO FRAGMENTS (end of week)
- Wins: quick instrument rollout was straightforward; we caught a TTL mismatch that explained some cache misses.
- Misses: over-ambitious on refactor scope — stalled reviews. Need smaller carve-outs next time.
- Experiment outcome (mini-audit): TTL bump in staging -> KV hit-rate +3.2%; tail latency improvement small but consistent (~3%). Not yet at target.

OPEN QUESTIONS
- Is the TTL bump safe across dedicated pools with heterogeneous workloads? (ask @platform-engineering)
- Will increasing logging volume meaningfully affect throughput at peak? Need an SLI estimate.
- Is the adaptive-batching gate orthogonal to model-quantization changes planned in Optimize? (link to consult: https://confluence.redwood/optimize/quantization-roadmap)

IMMERSION / FOCUS SLOTS (my lightweight ritual)
- Slot template (60–90m)
  - 0–10m: quick intent + ticket + branch check
  - 10–70m: deep work (no Slack, set DND)
  - 70–90m: commit + tiny note to this doc + plan next slot
- Aim: 4 slots/week minimum. Track slots as small ticks in calendar (focused-block).

NOTES TO SELF (short bullets)
- Stop adding more scope to a slot; if PR grows, break it and schedule another slot.
- When blocked >1 slot, escalate with a 15-min sync.
- Keep customer-facing language simple: what happened, why, and a one-line mitigation.

REFERENCES / LINKS
- Confluence playbook: https://confluence.redwood/ENG/serve-latency-playbook
- Related Jira: JIRA-ENG-2345 (cache audit), JIRA-CS-101 (customer ticket)
- Draft PR: github.com/redwood/infra/pull/812

NEXT STEPS (this week)
- Monday: push cache instrumentation to canary; monitor KV hit-rate.
- Wednesday: split refactor into PR A/B; open PR A and request small review from Maya.
- Friday: synthesize slot outcomes, update this doc with any metric deltas, and decide go/no-go on larger TTL change.

END NOTES (scratchpad)
- Use "garden" mental model: prune (remove cruft), sow (plant small experiments), water (nurture good signals), harvest (capture wins & ship).
- Keep this doc light; transfer finished notes into confluence summary when something becomes important for the team.

-- Anna
